title: C# and .NET: which APIs and defaults turn into vulnerabilities?
short: Move off .NET 8 and 9 before support ends on 10 November 2026, never let data pick the type it deserializes into, and require authentication by default.
answer: Move every app off .NET 8 and 9 to .NET 10.0.14 or later now, since both lose support on 10 November 2026[^support][^oob], and before your next release remove `BinaryFormatter`, keep Json.NET's `TypeNameHandling` at `None` and set a fallback authorization policy. Judge everything else by whether outside data can pick a type, reach SQL text, a command line, a file path, a URL or raw HTML, or skip an authorization check.
audience: Developers and tech leads writing production C# on .NET and ASP.NET Core, including legacy .NET Framework code, and the security people who review it

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Move to .NET 10 and patch every month.
items.text: .NET 8 and 9 lose support on 10 November 2026; .NET 10 is supported until 14 November 2028[^support]. October's update fixed 44 CVEs[^net1013], and two fixes were only complete in 10.0.14 on 25 October[^oob]. Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines.

items.title: Deserialize only into types you name.
items.text: `BinaryFormatter` can't be made secure[^bfsec], and in 2026 CISA listed four exploited deserialization flaws in SharePoint alone[^kev]. Use System.Text.Json, and keep Json.NET's `TypeNameHandling` at `None`[^owaspdeser].

items.title: Require authentication by default, then check each record.
items.text: The fallback policy is `null`, so endpoints without authorization metadata are public[^authz]. Set it to `RequireAuthenticatedUser()`, mark public endpoints `[AllowAnonymous]` and call `IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync` on the record[^owaspdotnet]. Missing authorization ranks 4th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe].

items.title: Keep input out of SQL text, command lines and paths.
items.text: Use LINQ or `FromSql`, not `FromSqlRaw` with input in the string[^efsql], and `ArgumentList` with no shell[^owaspcmd]. SQL injection, path traversal and OS command injection rank 2nd, 6th and 9th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe].

items.title: Turn on the security analyzers and package audit.
items.text: Only some analysis rules run by default[^msbuild]: set `<AnalysisModeSecurity>All</AnalysisModeSecurity>`. NuGet Audit checks transitive packages by default only from `net10.0`, so set `<NuGetAuditMode>all</NuGetAuditMode>` elsewhere[^nugetaudit].

items.title: Where does outside data enter?
items.text: Find the controllers, minimal API handlers, Razor Pages, Blazor components, SignalR hubs and queue consumers it touches. Each should bind a request type, not an EF Core entity; see the api-security sheet.

items.title: Who may call it, on which record?
items.text: Ask why for every `[AllowAnonymous]`, `AllowAnonymous()`, `DisableAntiforgery()` and `[IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]`. Neither `[Authorize]` nor the fallback policy checks the record[^owaspdotnet].

items.title: Does input reach a type name, SQL, a process or a path?
Does it reach HTML or the network?
items.text: Check `Html.Raw`, `MarkupString`, `HttpClient` calls to URLs from input and every `ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback`.

items.title: Does it switch off the runtime's checks?
items.text: `unsafe` blocks, `Unsafe` and `MemoryMarshal` calls, `[DllImport]` and `[LibraryImport]` need a second reviewer and a test.

blocks.title: C# and .NET traps and what to use instead
items: **`BinaryFormatter` and its relatives.** `SoapFormatter`, `NetDataContractSerializer`, `LosFormatter` and `ObjectStateFormatter` also let the payload pick any type[^bfsec]. .NET 9 throws on `BinaryFormatter`, but the `System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters` package restores it, risks included[^bfmig]. Migrate to System.Text.Json; read old payloads with the NRBF reader, which doesn't create the encoded types[^bfmig].

**Json.NET `TypeNameHandling` other than `None`.** The JSON then names the .NET type to create, and Newtonsoft says to vet it with a custom `SerializationBinder`[^newtonsoft]. Keep `None`, and never pass `Type.GetType(name)` with a name from data to any serializer[^owaspdeser]. For polymorphic JSON, declare subtypes with System.Text.Json's `[JsonDerivedType]`.

**Known `machineKey` values in ASP.NET Framework.** Microsoft found over 3,000 publicly disclosed keys usable for ViewState code injection, one used to install the Godzilla post-exploitation framework[^mskeys], and CISA lists Sitecore's default keys as exploited[^kev]. Generate unique keys, rotate them and encrypt the `machineKey` section of `web.config`[^mskeys].

**`FromSqlRaw($"... {id}")`.** `FromSqlRaw` and `ExecuteSqlRaw` paste interpolated values into the SQL; `FromSql` and `ExecuteSql` send each `{value}` as a `DbParameter`[^efsql]. EF Core 10 warns on concatenation in raw SQL calls[^ef10]. Map column and table names from a fixed list[^owaspdotnet].

**`Process.Start("cmd.exe", "/c ...")`.** `UseShellExecute` defaults to `true` on .NET Framework[^useshell]. Set it to `false`, use a fixed full path, add each value to `ArgumentList`, and never pass input to `cmd.exe`, `powershell.exe` or `sh -c`. .NET Framework has no `ArgumentList`: accept only values that need no quoting[^owaspcmd].

**`Path.Combine(root, name)`.** A rooted `name` discards `root`, and Microsoft says to use `Path.Join` for user input[^pathcombine]. That still lets `..` climb out, so require `Path.GetFullPath()` of the result to start with the root plus a separator.

**`HttpClient.GetAsync(url)` with a URL from input.** Server-side request forgery ranks 22nd in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Allowlist hosts, check the resolved address in `SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback`, and set `AllowAutoRedirect = false`: redirects are followed by default[^redirect]. CA5359 flags certificate checks turned off[^secrules].

**`Html.Raw`, `HtmlString` and `MarkupString`.** They skip Razor's encoding[^owaspdotnet][^blazor], and cross-site scripting ranks 1st in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Sanitize user HTML with a maintained sanitizer; HTML encoding doesn't protect values inside JavaScript or URLs[^owaspdotnet].

**`JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>()` with default options.** Nullable annotations are compile-time only[^nrt], so a `string Name` can arrive `null`, and a repeated property overwrites the first[^net10lib]. In .NET 10, `JsonSerializerOptions.Strict` rejects unknown and duplicate properties and honors nullable annotations[^net10lib].

blocks.title: Tools that catch it
items: **.NET analyzers.** `<AnalysisModeSecurity>All</AnalysisModeSecurity>` enables every security rule as a warning, and `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` fails the build on them[^msbuild]. Start with CA2300 to CA2330 (deserializers), CA2100 and CA3001 (SQL), CA3006 (processes), CA3003 (paths) and CA5394 (`Random`)[^secrules].
**BannedApiAnalyzers.** Add `T:System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters.Binary.BinaryFormatter` and other APIs you ban to `BannedSymbols.txt`, and builds warn on each use[^banned].
**CodeQL.** `cs/unsafe-deserialization-untrusted-input`, `cs/sql-injection`, `cs/command-line-injection`, `cs/path-injection` and `cs/zipslip`[^codeql].

**NuGet Audit.** It runs on every restore. Make NU1903 and NU1904 (high, critical) errors with `<WarningsAsErrors>` and run `dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive` in CI[^nugetaudit]. The supply-chain sheet covers the rest.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **.NET 8 and 9 reach end of support on 10 November**[^support], and .NET Framework 4.6.2 on 12 January 2027[^fwlife].

**October brought 44 .NET CVEs,** among them critical Kestrel request smuggling (CVE-2026-88092, CVSS 9.4)[^net1013][^kestrel]. Two fixes were incomplete until 10.0.14, 9.0.22 and 8.0.33 on 25 October[^oob].

**Data Protection let attackers forge auth cookies.** CVE-2026-40372 (CVSS 9.1) hit packages 10.0.0 to 10.0.6. If you ran them exposed, update, rotate the key ring and replace tokens issued in the window[^dataprot].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **`SecureString`.** Microsoft advises against it for new code, and it isn't encrypted outside Windows[^securestring]. Keep secrets in a vault and out of logs.
**A `SerializationBinder` to tame `BinaryFormatter`.** Microsoft says it may not stop code execution and doesn't commit to patching bypasses[^bfsec]. Migrate instead.
**In-process sandboxes.** Code Access Security and partial trust aren't supported security boundaries[^owaspdotnet]. Run untrusted code in its own process or container.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Patching the server but not the app.** Self-contained apps stay vulnerable until recompiled and redeployed[^kestrel], and standalone packages need their own update[^oob]. Rebuild container images on every .NET patch.

**Leaving Data Protection keys unprotected.** Default storage encrypts keys only on Windows, not on Azure App Service, and naming your own key store turns that off[^dpkeys]. Encrypt them with `ProtectKeysWithAzureKeyVault` and keep them out of the image.
**Shipping development settings.** Run production outside the `Development` environment, and keep User Secrets, which aren't encrypted, for development[^owaspdotnet].

blocks.title: What this looks like for your code

columns.title: New project
items: Start on .NET 10 with `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`, `<AnalysisModeSecurity>All</AnalysisModeSecurity>` and warnings as errors.
Set the fallback policy before the first endpoint.
Ban `BinaryFormatter` in `BannedSymbols.txt` from the first commit.

columns.title: Existing codebase
items: Leave .NET 8 and 9 now, and move .NET Framework 4.6.2 apps to 4.8.1 before 12 January 2027[^fwlife].
Search for `BinaryFormatter`, `TypeNameHandling`, `FromSqlRaw`, `Process.Start` and `Html.Raw`.
Set `<NuGetAuditMode>all</NuGetAuditMode>` in `Directory.Build.props` below `net10.0`.

columns.title: High-assurance or regulated
items: Make CodeQL's `security-extended` suite a required check.
Turn on `CheckForOverflowUnderflow` where code computes sizes or money.
Keep one Key Vault-protected key ring per app and rehearse revoking it[^dataprot].
